method: read the actual Salsa source directly (not the project's own book/README) -- revision.rs (Revision/AtomicRevision), durability.rs (the 4-level Durability enum and its own doc comment stating the exact optimization rationale), zalsa_local.rs (QueryRevisions: changed_at/durability/origin_and_extra), function/memo.rs (MemoHeader.verified_at), and function/maybe_changed_after.rs (shallow_verify_memo_cold, the actual shallow-then-deep two-tier verification algorithm) -- following this session's own established genome-record methodology (per blake3-content-addressing.md's own precedent: capability/problem, semantic mechanism with real line-citations, required invariants, identity/scope model, and an explicit Decision separating essential mechanism from accidental implementation detail).
key_finding: Salsa's core mechanism is a two-tier verification algorithm, not memoization alone: (1) an O(1) 'shallow' check comparing a per-durability-level last-changed-revision counter against a memo's own verified_at timestamp -- if nothing at or below the memo's own minimum input durability has changed, the entire dependency graph walk is skipped outright; (2) only on shallow-check failure, an O(dependency-subgraph-size) 'deep' walk recursively re-verifying each individually-recorded dependency. Separately, each memo tracks verified_at (last confirmed valid) DISTINCT from changed_at (last actually changed) -- letting a query's own dependents avoid re-running when an ancestor was merely re-verified without its value changing ('backdating'). This maps directly onto R5's six declared required capabilities, evidenced with real source citations rather than inferred from the library's reputation.
